itinerary: Day 1: Arrival in Islamabad, hotel transfer and welcome dinner
Day 2: Fly to Skardu with scenic mountain views
Day 3: Skardu city tour, Kharpocho fort hike, shopping
Day 4: Drive to Askoli, 5-7 hour jeep through Shigar Valley
Day 10: Trek to Concordia, the Throne Room of Mountain Gods
Day 11: Trek to Broad Peak and K2 Base Camp
Day 12: Begin return, retracing route through glacier camps
Day 13: Return trek down glacier camps
Day 14: Return trek down glacier camps
Day 15: Return trek to Askoli area
Day 18: Fly to Islamabad (drive if flight cancelled)
pros: Transparent tiered pricing for solo/2-4/6+/8+ groups and separate Pakistani-national rates
Straightforward Concordia out-and-back to both K2 and Broad Peak Base Camps, no risky pass crossing
Built-in flight-cancellation fallback (alternative drive) on the final day
Satellite phone for emergencies included
Local Skardu-based operator with local staff emphasis
cons: Porter weight allowance only 14 kg for personal luggage
No dedicated acclimatization rest day; relies on natural trekking progression
Permit fees stated as included but no royalty/CKNP breakdown shown
Insurance, visa, tips and personal gear all excluded
verdict: Best for budget-conscious trekkers who want a no-frills, classic Concordia/K2BC out-and-back with clear group-size pricing; less ideal for those wanting a structured acclimatization plan or a Gondogoro La finish.
excludes: Travel insurance, Pakistan visa, international airfare, personal equipment (boots/jackets), tips/gratuities and miscellaneous expenses.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrival at Islamabad, transfer to hotel (540m)
Day 2: Flight to Skardu, Himalaya/Karakoram views (2230m)
Day 3: Rest/acclimatization day at Skardu, Kharpocho hike
Day 4: Drive to Askoli, 5-7 hour jeep (3000m)
Day 7: Rest day at Paju for acclimatization
Day 11: Trek to Concordia, Throne Room of Mountain Gods (4691m)
Day 12: Trek to K2 Base Camp (5117m)
Day 15: Cross Gondogoro La, camp at Khuspang
pros: Two acclimatization/rest days built in (Skardu Day 3 and Paju Day 7)
Includes the scenic Gondogoro La crossing (5585m) so it is a one-way loop, not a backtrack
Generous extras: boiled water, snacks, cookies and dry fruit daily on trek
Can hire a native-language guide for private groups (e.g. Spanish/Chinese speakers)
Permit, waste-management, toll and bridge fees all bundled into price
cons: Gondogoro La is a glaciated, crampon/harness pass crossing, harder and riskier than a straight Concordia trek
Porter weight allowance only 15 kg for personal luggage
Personal technical gear (ice axe, crampons, harness, helmet) excluded unless arranged on request
21-day itinerary is long and prices vary widely by date ($2,000-$4,500)
verdict: Best for fit, adventurous trekkers who want the full K2 Base Camp plus Gondogoro La pass crossing rather than an out-and-back; this is a tougher, technical-edge itinerary, not a beginner Concordia walk.
excludes: Personal insurance, Pakistan visa and fees, international flights, personal clothing and technical equipment, extra hotel stays, tips, and anything not in the listed inclusions.

itinerary: Day 1: Arrival day in Islamabad, Pakistan
Day 2: Islamabad to Skardu flight, 45 min (2230m)
Day 3: Sightseeing and preparation day, Skardu
Day 4: Skardu to Johla via Askole
Day 5: Trek (Baltoro approach, per detailed itinerary)
Day 7: Trek continues up the glacier
Day 8: Acclimatization and rest day at Urdukas
Day 9: Trek further along Baltoro Glacier
Day 11: Concordia / K2 Base Camp area
Day 20: Departure day - fly back home
pros: Long-established local Pakistani company operating ~40 years
Dedicated acclimatization and rest day at Urdukas (Day 8)
Small groups capped at twelve people
Porter wages and insurance included (helicopter rescue excluded)
Fully refundable $170 deposit and clear $2,055 base price
cons: Permit/CKNP fees are excluded extras (trekking permit $150, CKNP fee $190)
Seasonal price swing is wide ($1,790-$3,900)
Porter limit 18 kg per traveller is stated but personal kit still your responsibility
Travel insurance and visa fees excluded
verdict: Best for trekkers who value a deeply experienced local operator with explicit acclimatization and small-group caps, and who are comfortable paying permit/CKNP fees on top of the base price.
excludes: Travel insurance, Pakistan visa fees, trekking permit ($150) and CKNP fees ($190), tips, sightseeing tours and miscellaneous expenses.

itinerary: Day 1: Islamabad/Rawalpindi arrival and city tour (540m)
Day 2: Fly Islamabad to Skardu, road fallback via Babusar (2228m)
Day 3: Free/preparation day in Skardu, bazaar and fort
Day 4: Drive Skardu to Askoli, 6-7 hour jeep (3000m)
Day 7: Free day at Paiyu for local exploration/acclimatization
Day 12: Trek to K2 Base Camp (5150m)
Day 13: Begin return trek toward Skardu
pros: Detailed, well-paced 20-day itinerary with a free/acclimatization day at Paiyu (Day 7)
Strong inclusions: D3V sleeping tent, toilet tent, shower tent, first-aid kit, satellite phone
Government permit fees and waste-management fees included in price
Road fallback via Babusar Pass if the Skardu flight is cancelled
Established, licensed local operator (29 years, Govt Licence 396; Hunza HQ + Islamabad office)
cons: Porter limit 15 kg for personal luggage
Sleeping bag excluded (must bring your own despite tents being provided)
Single-supplement charged separately; headline price ($2,085) lower than the $2,620 per-person group rate
Insurance, visa and tips all excluded
verdict: Best for trekkers wanting a transparent, full-service local outfit with permits/waste fees bundled and good camp comforts; a solid standard Concordia/K2BC out-and-back rather than a pass crossing.
excludes: International airfare/taxes, Pakistan visa and personal insurance, tips, single supplement, sleeping bag, personal expenses and gratuities, and any service not listed.

itinerary: Day 7: Acclimatization rest day at Paiju
Day 11: Trek to K2 Base Camp (5100m) / Broad Peak BC
Day 12: K2 and Broad Peak Base Camp area
Day 13: Begin return down the glacier
pros: Acclimatization rest day at Paiju (Day 7)
Domestic flights include 20kg checked baggage allowance
CKNP Waste Management Fee (USD 150) is bundled into the price
Discounted headline price ($2,290 from $2,900)
Pakistan-based with head office in Islamabad
cons: Government permit fee (USD 150-300) is an excluded extra
Some meals excluded on trek (5 lunches and 6 dinners not covered)
Porter limit only 14 kg per person
Personal travel insurance, international airfare and visa all excluded
verdict: Best for value-seekers who want a discounted standard K2/Broad Peak Base Camp out-and-back and don't mind that the government permit and several trail meals are billed separately.
excludes: International airfare and visa, personal travel insurance, government permit fee (USD 150-300), 5 lunches and 6 dinners, and tips/gratuities for guides, porters and staff.

itinerary: Day 13: Trek to Broad Peak Base Camp
Day 14: Trek to K2 Base Camp, Gilkey Memorial visit
Day 15: K2 Base Camp area / exploration
pros: All permit fees AND liaison officer costs are included (rare among operators)
Full base camp setup: dining tents, showers, bathroom, solar charger, satellite phone
Built-in reserve weather days (Days 24-25) for flight/weather contingencies
Optional Gondogoro La crossing offered for stronger trekkers
Three meals/day on trek, base camp and mountain
cons: Far more expensive at $5,850 fixed, roughly double local operators
Foreign-led (Dan Mazur, British/American) with only a local Balti agent for ground coordination
No group-size pricing tiers offered
No porter weight limit or detailed acclimatization schedule published
verdict: Best for Western trekkers who want a foreign-led, fully-supported expedition with permits and liaison officers handled and built-in weather buffer, and who will pay a premium for it; overkill for budget-minded trekkers.
excludes: International flights to Islamabad, trekking rescue and travel insurance, personal climbing/trekking equipment, and Pakistan visa.

itinerary: Day 6: Trek up the Baltoro approach
Day 12: Optional K2 Base Camp visit (5150m), return to Concordia
Day 13: Begin return trek down glacier
pros: Describes the route honestly as non-technical, gentle glacier travel (good expectation-setting)
Provides a Letter of Invitation (LOI) to help obtain the Pakistan tourist visa
Local Pakistan-based operator (Islamabad and Hunza offices, ~15 years, licence DTS:1994)
Classic safe Concordia out-and-back with optional K2BC day, no risky pass crossing
cons: No price published on the page
No porter weight limit, acclimatization schedule, or permit/royalty fees disclosed
Hotel accommodation only covers 9 nights (twin-sharing) against 14 nights camping
Tips, bottled water and alcohol excluded
verdict: Best for trekkers prioritizing a relaxed, non-technical Concordia route with visa LOI support from an established local operator, but transparency is weak: no pricing, porter limits, or permit detail is published, so confirm directly.
excludes: International flights, airport/departure taxes and visa fee, personal items, tips for guides/drivers/porters, bottled water and alcohol.
